source.author: verg
source.text: Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_original: 'Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis / lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra / spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus / mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_english: First, within the heavens, the lands, the watery plains, the shining orb of the Moon, and the Titanian stars, a spirit nourishes all things from within; poured through its limbs, mind stirs the whole mass and mingles itself with the great body.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quem secutus Virgilius ait: Deum namque ire per omnes Terrasque tractusque maris, etc.; et: Principio coelum ac terras, camposque liquentes, Lucentemque globum lunae, Titaniaque astra, Spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet.
reuse.text_original: Quem secutus Virgilius ait: Deum namque ire per omnes Terrasque tractusque maris, etc.; et: Principio coelum ac terras, camposque liquentes, Lucentemque globum lunae, Titaniaque astra, Spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet.
reuse.text_english: Whom Virgil followed when he said: For God, indeed, goes through all the lands and the tracts of the sea, etc.; and: First, he nourishes within all things, the heaven and the earth, the watery plains, and the shining orb of the moon and Titan’s stars; the spirit within feeds them all, and a mind, poured through the limbs, moves the whole mass and mingles with the great body.
